title: Sink-Free Attention Enables Prefix-Free Streaming KV Caches

contributions.purpose: Show that gated attention allows stable streaming inference without preserving prefix sink tokens in the KV cache.
contributions.mechanism: Compare vanilla and gated Qwen2-1B models under pure rolling-window (0+W) versus prefix-sink (S+(W-S)) cache regimes with cache-relative positional encoding.
contributions.evaluation: Gated attention achieves a PPL ratio of 1.015-1.007 between pure rolling-window and prefix-sink regimes, versus 2.54 for vanilla attention.
contributions.domain: streaming LLM inference / KV cache management
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that gated attention achieves prefix-free streaming stability, with a PPL ratio of 1.015-1.007 between pure rolling-window and prefix-sink regimes, compared to 2.54 for vanilla attention.

contributions.purpose: Establish the causal mechanism linking gating to streaming stability via attention sink elimination.
contributions.mechanism: Measure attention sink rate under post-SDPA gating and correlate low sink rate with stable streaming across all tested models.
contributions.evaluation: Gating reduces attention sink rate by 99.3-100%, and low sink rate perfectly predicts stable streaming across all tested models.
contributions.source_quote: We verify the causal mechanism: gating reduces attention sink rate by 99.3-100%, and low sink rate perfectly predicts stable streaming across all tested models.

contributions.purpose: Rule out model degradation as an alternative explanation for the streaming stability gains.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluate full-attention perplexity of gated versus baseline models to confirm gated models are not simply weaker.
contributions.evaluation: Gated models maintain comparable or slightly better full-attention perplexity (12.71-12.79 vs 12.82 baseline).
contributions.source_quote: We confirm that streaming stability gains are genuine—gated models maintain comparable or slightly better full-attention perplexity (12.71-12.79 vs 12.82 baseline), ruling out model degradation as an explanation.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work differs by eliminating the need for prefix sink tokens entirely through gated attention, simplifying streaming deployment.
Our work leverages the sink-elimination property of gated attention (Qiu et al., 2025) to enable prefix-free streaming KV caches.
Our approach is orthogonal to these optimizations and can be combined with them for further efficiency gains.
Following StreamingLLM (Xiao et al., 2023), we use cache-relative positional encoding to avoid out-of-distribution absolute positions in both regimes.

notes: All three contributions are empirical findings (hypothesis test of gated attention from Qiu et al. 2025 in a streaming setting) rather than a new method. Experiments limited to Qwen2-1B scale.
